title: Shuffles of permutations in cycle form

definitions.name: x2611_15723_descents
definitions.notes: One-based descent positions. Fin n represents the paper's [n] by shifting labels down by one.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_des
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15723_des {n : ℕ} (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  (x2611_15723_descents π).card

definitions.name: x2611_15723_maj
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15723_maj {n : ℕ} (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  (x2611_15723_descents π).sum id
definitions.notes: Major index, with the original one-based positions.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_cycleShuffle
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15723_cycleShuffle {k l : ℕ}
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin l)) :
    Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin (k + l))) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter (fun π =>
    ∃ (e : Fin k ↪o Fin (k + l)) (f : Fin l ↪o Fin (k + l)),
      Disjoint (Set.range e) (Set.range f) ∧
      Set.range e ∪ Set.range f = Set.univ ∧
      (∀ i, π (e i) = e (σ i)) ∧ (∀ j, π (f j) = f (τ j)))
definitions.notes: Definition 1.1 via the printed equivalent invariant-subset description. The increasing embeddings are the standardizations of the two complementary invariant subsets.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_shuffle
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15723_shuffle {k l : ℕ}
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin l)) :
    Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin (k + l))) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter (fun π =>
    (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => (σ i).val)).Sublist
      (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (k + l) => (π i).val)) ∧
    (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin l => k + (τ j).val)).Sublist
      (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (k + l) => (π i).val)))
definitions.notes: The usual shuffle of the one-line word of σ with the word of τ shifted by k.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_noOrderIso
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15723_noOrderIso {k l : ℕ}
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin l)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Fin k) (b : Fin l),
    ¬ ∃ e : {x : Fin k // σ.SameCycle a x} ≃o
        {y : Fin l // τ.SameCycle b y},
      ∀ x y : {z : Fin k // σ.SameCycle a z},
        σ x.val = y.val → τ (e x).val = (e y).val
definitions.notes: No cycle of σ is order-isomorphic to a cycle of τ. An order isomorphism of orbit supports must intertwine the permutations. SameCycle includes fixed-point singleton cycles.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_qchoose
definitions.notes: Gaussian binomial polynomial evaluated at q, defined by the k-subset formula. This polynomial definition includes q = 0, 1 and roots of unity without a quotient singularity.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_zchoose
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15723_zchoose (n k : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  if 0 ≤ n ∧ 0 ≤ k then Nat.choose n.toNat k.toNat else 0
definitions.notes: Ordinary binomial coefficient with signed indices, zero for negative lower indices or negative upper indices. The upper indices in Corollary 1.7 are nonnegative.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_fundamental
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15723_fundamental (m n : ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ)
    (x : Fin m → ℚ) : ℚ :=
  ∑ w : Fin n → Fin m,
    if Monotone w ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin n, j.val = i.val + 1 → i.val + 1 ∈ J → w i < w j)
    then ∏ i : Fin n, x (w i) else 0
definitions.notes: Finite-alphabet evaluation F_{n,J}(x_1,...,x_m,0,...), with weakly increasing indices and strict rises at J. Requiring identities for every m and every rational x is equivalent to the printed homogeneous formal-series identities.

definitions.name: x2611_15723_psi
definitions.notes: The operator Ψ on a fundamental function, viewed as a power series in t after rational specialization of q. Its t^m coefficient is F_{n,J}(1,q,...,q^{m-1},0,...).

statements.label: Section 1.1, cardinality with no order-isomorphic cycles
statements.name: x2611_15723_cycleShuffle_card
statements.original: We first investigate the case when no cycle of $\sigma$ is order-isomorphic to a cycle of $\tau$ ; we say that $\sigma$ and $\tau$ have no order-isomorphic cycles. In this case, we have $|\sigma\shuffle_{c}\tau|=\binom{n}{k}$ , since $\pi\in\sigma\shuffle_{c}\tau$ is uniquely determined by the partition $[n]=K\sqcup L$ .

statements.notes: The hypothesis compares all orbit cycles, including singleton fixed-point cycles. The ambient size is k+l.

statements.label: Theorem 1.6
statements.name: x2611_15723_thm1_6
statements.original:
For every $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{k}$ and $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_{n-k}$ with no order-isomorphic cycles,

 $\sum_{\pi\in\sigma\shuffle_{c}\tau}F_{n,\Des(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi^{\prime}\in\sigma\shuffle\tau}F_{n,\Des(\pi^{\prime})}.$ 

(1)

Equivalently, for any pair $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{k}$ and $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_{n-k}$ with no order-isomorphic cycles,
the statistic $\Des$ has the same distribution on the set of
shuffles-by-cycle
 $\sigma\shuffle_{c}\tau$ as on the set of standard shuffles $\sigma\shuffle\tau$ .
statements.lean:
(k l : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin l))
    (h : x2611_15723_noOrderIso σ τ) (J : Finset ℕ) :
  ((x2611_15723_cycleShuffle σ τ).filter
      (fun π => x2611_15723_descents π = J)).card =
    ((x2611_15723_shuffle σ τ).filter
      (fun π => x2611_15723_descents π = J)).card
statements.notes: Uses the equivalently clause printed immediately after equation (1), namely equality of the descent-set distributions. J ranges over all finite sets of one-based positions. Sets outside the possible descent range have empty fibers on both sides.

fidelity.twin: (n k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n - k))) (h : x2611_15723_noOrderIso σ τ) : ∀ (m : ℕ) (x : Fin m → ℚ), (∑ π ∈ x2611_15723_cycleShuffle σ τ, x2611_15723_fundamental m n (x2611_15723_descents π) x) = ∑ π ∈ x2611_15723_shuffle σ τ, x2611_15723_fundamental m n (x2611_15723_descents π) x

statements.label: Corollary 1.7
statements.name: x2611_15723_cor1_7
statements.original:
For every $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{k}$ and $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_{n-k}$ with no order-isomorphic cycles,

 $\sum_{\pi\in\sigma\shuffle_{c}\tau}q^{\maj(\pi)}=q^{\maj(\sigma)+\maj(\tau)}{{n}\brack{k}}_{q}$ 

and

 $\sum_{\pi\in\sigma\shuffle_{c}\tau}t^{\des(\pi)}=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\binom{k+\des(\tau)-\des(\sigma)}{i-\des(\sigma)}\binom{n-k+\des(\sigma)-\des(\tau)}{i-\des(\tau)}\,t^{i}.$

  (∑ π ∈ x2611_15723_cycleShuffle σ τ, t ^ x2611_15723_des π) =

Polynomial identities are expressed for every rational q and t, which is equivalent to their formal polynomial versions over ℚ. The Gaussian binomial uses its polynomial subset formula.

statements.label: Theorem 1.12
statements.name: x2611_15723_thm1_12
statements.lean:
(n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (hσ : σ.IsCycleOn Set.univ) (q t : ℚ) :
  (∑ π ∈ x2611_15723_cycleShuffle σ σ,
      q ^ x2611_15723_maj π * t ^ x2611_15723_des π) =
    q ^ (2 * x2611_15723_maj σ) * t ^ x2611_15723_des σ *
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),

statements.notes: The paper's n-cycle hypothesis is represented by positive n and transitivity on all of Fin n. IsCycleOn includes the n=1 singleton cycle. statements.label: Corollary 1.14
statements.name: x2611_15723_cor1_14
statements.original:
For every cycle $\sigma\in\mathcal{C}_{(n)}$ ,

 $\sum_{\pi\in\sigma\shuffle_{c}\sigma}t^{\des(\pi)}=t^{\des(\sigma)}\cdot\sum_{i=0}^{n}a_{i,n}t^{i},$ 

where

 $a_{i,n}=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\binom{\binom{n}{i}+1}{2},&\ \text{if $i$ is even};\\
{}\\
\displaystyle\binom{\binom{n}{i}}{2},&\ \text{if $i$ is odd}.\end{cases}$
statements.lean:
(n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))

    t ^ x2611_15723_des σ *
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
        ((if Even i then Nat.choose (Nat.choose n i + 1) 2
          else Nat.choose (Nat.choose n i) 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) * t ^ i
statements.notes: The piecewise coefficients a_{i,n} are expanded in place, preserving the printed parity convention. Uses the positive n-cycle convention and universal rational specialization of the polynomial variable.

statements.notes: The rational expression is multiplied by its denominator (t;q)_{n+1}, whose constant coefficient is 1, so this is equivalent in formal power series. q is universally specialized to ℚ, and t is PowerSeries.X. This literal ℕ transcription allows n=0 and J=∅, where the printed identity fails. A positive-degree convention would exclude that boundary case.
